text: [See David Kleis, Inc. v. Sup.Ct. (California Ins. Co.) (1995) 37 CA4th 1035, 1047-1048, 44 CR2d 181, 188-189] b. [3:445] Coverage under CGL “personal injury liability” coverage? Although sexual harassment is not one of the enumerated “personal injury offenses,” allegations of sexual misconduct may disclose a potential for coverage under one of the recognized “offenses”—particularly, false imprisonment or detention (see ¶ 3:298). As noted by one court: “The fact that the victim construed the activity as sexual misconduct, and filed a claim on that basis, does not preclude a jury from finding that no sexual harassment took place but that a false imprisonment or detention did occur.” [David Kleis, Inc. v. Sup.Ct. (California Ins. Co.), supra, 37 CA4th at 1050, 44 CR2d at 190 (emphasis added)] c. [3:446] “Intentional injury” exclusion: CGL bodily injury coverage may also be excluded because the victim's injuries are deemed “expected or intended by the insured” (see ¶ 3:311). d.
